name: Timer Switch
tagline: A switch that works to a clock instead of a finger — outdoor lighting that goes off on its own.
terminals: L — permanent live to power the timer
N — neutral, needed by the electronics or the clock motor
Load — switched live out to the lamp
Earth — plate earth on metal plates
parts: Faceplate — usually a deeper plate than a plain switch
Dial or digital display — the programme you set
Override / boost button — forces the output on for the rest of the set period
Selector — ON / AUTO / OFF on mechanical timers
Rear terminals, including the neutral the electronics need
safety: A timer needs a neutral, so it will not replace a plain switch on a two-plate lighting circuit without a new cable. Outdoor lighting must be RCD-protected, and the enclosure and fittings need an IP rating that suits the location.

points.label: Faceplate
points.detail: Deeper than a plain switch because the mechanism or electronics sit behind the plate. Check the back box depth before you buy — a 25 mm box rarely takes a timer.

points.label: Dial and pointer
points.detail: The dial carries the time scale and the set segments; the pointer is the clock. On a mechanical timer the tappets you push out are the on and off times; on an electronic one the same information is a programme in memory, which is why it survives a power cut only if the unit has a backup cell.

points.label: Override button
points.detail: Forces the output on — a boost that either runs for a fixed period (typically one or two hours) or until the next programmed off time. It is the control you use at the door without having to reprogramme anything.

points.label: Selector (ON / AUTO / OFF)
points.detail: ON holds the load live permanently, OFF holds it off, and AUTO hands control to the clock. Leaving a timer on ON is the usual reason a “timed” light is found burning at midday.

points.label: Fixing screws
points.detail: Two screws into the back box, as for any plate accessory. Do not trap the neutral conductor behind the plate when you push the unit home.
